title: Markdown heading
rationale: Removes the visual heading marker because Kokoro can announce it as header or subheader.

title: One announcement for an unordered list
rationale: Removes visual bullet markers so symbol choice cannot leak into speech.
originalText:
- Keep the original voice.
- Restore the clipboard.
- Preserve normal hotkeys.
expectedPreparedText:
Keep the original voice.
Restore the clipboard.
Preserve normal hotkeys.

title: One announcement for a numbered list
rationale: Leaves numbered lists alone because Kokoro already reads their numbers naturally.
originalText:
1. Select some text.
2. Press the hotkey.
3. Press it again to stop.
expectedPreparedText:
1. Select some text.
2. Press the hotkey.
3. Press it again to stop.

title: Checklist syntax
rationale: Removes checklist syntax without announcing either the list or the visual checked state.
originalText:
- [x] Kokoro is installed.
- [ ] Start with Windows is enabled.
expectedPreparedText:
Kokoro is installed.
Start with Windows is enabled.

title: One announcement for a blockquote
rationale: Announces a contiguous quote once instead of repeating quote before every line.
originalText:
> The first quoted sentence remains intact.
> The second sentence continues the same quotation.
expectedPreparedText:
Quote. The first quoted sentence remains intact.
The second sentence continues the same quotation.

title: Hard-wrapped prose
rationale: Keeps the preferred removal of a visual line wrap that created an audible pause.
originalText:
This sentence was wrapped
across two visual lines before it reached Pulse Reader.
expectedPreparedText: This sentence was wrapped across two visual lines before it reached Pulse Reader.

title: Dash inside a URL
rationale: Expands the scheme colon and path dash Kokoro omitted while retaining the otherwise acceptable URL reading.
expectedPreparedText: Open https colon example.com/pulse dash reader/docs for details.

title: Dots and at-sign inside an email address
rationale: Expands punctuation only inside the detected address so its exact spelling is audible.
originalText: Send the report to reader.tests@example.org tomorrow.
expectedPreparedText: Send the report to reader dot tests at example dot org tomorrow.

title: File-extension dot
rationale: Expands the drive colon and final dot Kokoro omitted from the detected Windows path.
originalText: The model is stored at C:\Users\Reader\Models\kokoro.onnx.
expectedPreparedText: The model is stored at C colon \Users\Reader\Models\kokoro dot onnx.

title: Ellipsis as an explicit pause
rationale: Removes the noisy ellipsis phoneme and inserts a controlled longer pause between reading units.
originalText: Wait... is the next voice ready? Yes, it is.
expectedPreparedText: Wait is the next voice ready? Yes, it is.

title: British date and twenty-four-hour time
rationale: Adds the missing ordinal and removes the unnatural colon pause from an unambiguous format.
originalText: The test starts on 24 August 2026 at 14:35.
expectedPreparedText: The test starts on 24th of August 2026 at fourteen thirty-five.

title: Mathematical operators
rationale: Expands operators only after the text is confidently recognized as an expression.
originalText: The expression is x >= 10, and the result is y = x * 2.
expectedPreparedText: The expression is x is greater than or equal to 10, and the result is y equals x multiplied by 2.

title: Parsed JSON properties
rationale: Parses valid JSON and reads its values without braces, quotes, or other noisy syntax.

title: Code-block announcement
rationale: Replaces an unreliable partial reading with a short announcement and skips the code contents.

title: Fenced prose is not code
rationale: Removes the fence and reads its prose instead of falsely announcing a code block.
originalText:
```text
This is a quoted passage in a Markdown document.
It should still be read normally.
```
expectedPreparedText: This is a quoted passage in a Markdown document. It should still be read normally.

title: Table rows as sentences
rationale: Treats each row as one reading unit and uses semicolons for a moderate pause without splitting every cell into a separate utterance.
